title: Relative Performance Evaluation and Competitive Aggressiveness

scopes.description: Full supplied workflow: one native R data-preparation route followed by the substantive table-analysis program embedded in FMT-log-file-tables.pdf. FMT-create-data.pdf is a duplicate rendering of the preparation program, not a second required preparation stage. The final Data assembly/RData producer and some source-to-analysis variable handoffs remain unresolved.

software.name: R 4.5.0 with tidyverse, lubridate, broom, RPostgres, data.table, zoo, fixest and psych
software.description: R 4.5.0 is installed, but metadata-only inspection found none of the required packages. Native code calls fread and rollapplyr without explicit attachment; the table program loads fixest and calls psych::describe. No author code or packages were executed for trials.

issues.description: The cleaning block builds Ravenpack2 and selects the ten event-level fields consumed downstream, but the commented writer names the raw Ravenpack object. A source-hash-bound one-line writer change aligns that existing cleaned object with the exact basename read twice later. A compatible prepared cleaned file can instead bypass raw-building through setup; actual files, coverage and licensing remain unverified.

The native driver contains placeholder WRDS credentials, uses an undefined wrds2 connection for crsp_a_ccm.ccm_lookup, and later queries unqualified ccm_lookup. Frozen catalog hits are different CCMXPF history tables and do not expose all requested CUSIP/TIC/CIK fields; authorized connection, exact schemas, historical link selection and field mapping are unresolved.

The supplied code queries gvkey/gind from co_hgic and keeps the first returned row per GVKEY with distinct(GVKEY, .keep_all = TRUE); the frozen catalog labels co_hgic as a history table with indfrom/indthru. Preserve this literal authored row-selection behavior and record its source-order sensitivity as a fidelity limitation; no new current-versus-historical research choice is required to attempt the code as written.

The table program loads FMT-environment.RData and consumes Data, while the complete native preparation source ends at Overlap_match and contains no final Data assembly or environment save. The producer and variable lineage for the analysis-ready environment are not supplied; no RData object was deserialized or guessed at.
The native Peer_synchro function returns ACTUAL_IN and ACTUAL_OUT, but the table code requires PG_SYNCHRONICITY. No supported mapping, aggregation or final Data producer documents this measure.

Five active setwd calls contain literal ... placeholders in the RavenPack, Hoberg-Phillips, peer-match, incentive and overlap-match stages. The intended directories are not documented in the supplied source and need ordinary path configuration.

All required R packages checked are absent in the R 4.5.0 environment. The source also calls fread and rollapplyr without attaching their provider packages; install/setup and binding changes are needed before a future run.

The native ExecuComp assignment filters CEO rows but ends before the following transmute expression, so the intended uppercase GVKEY/FYEAR/TOTAL_COMP/CASH_COMP fields are not constructed by this handoff. Three downstream joins select those fields. Appending a pipe at line 1343 continues the existing CEO-filtered rows into the supplied transmute without changing its calculations; the duplicate preparation PDF shows the same break.

evidence.description: The documented sequence builds RavenPack actions, ISS peer data, Compustat fundamentals and Hoberg-Phillips measures, then merges datasets for analysis; the identifiers file is only firm-year IDs.
evidence.quote:
Step #1: Construct competitive aggressiveness data. We use RavenPack (ISIN) and
          Compustat identifier (GVKEY).

       Step #2: Construct relative performance plans and peer-related data. We use ISS Incentive
          Lab data and SEC identifier (CIK).

       Step #3: Construct relevant firm-level and industry-level fundamentals. We use Compustat
          and Compustat identifier (GVKEY).

       Step #4: Construct competitive environment variable. We use Hoberg-Phillips Library and
          Compustat identifier (GVKEY)

       Step #5: Merge all datasets for primary data analysis.

       Step #6: Begin analysis using final dataset.

       The accompanying “FMT-firm-identifiers” file contains the firm-year identifiers of all
       observations in our sample—Compustat identifier (GVKEY), SEC identifier (CIK) and
       fiscal year (FYEAR). The accompanying “FMT-create-data” and “FMT-log-file-tables”
       files contain R code to generate the variables and sample and tables, respectively. Please
       cite the paper if you use any of the code or data.

evidence.description: The native R driver joins annual Compustat fundamentals with dated Compustat industry SIC fields and derives GVKEY, CIK, FYEAR, date and SIC classifications.
evidence.quote:
##### IMPORT DATA: IDENTIFIERS #####
IDs <- left_join(x = dbSendQuery(wrds, "select gvkey, tic, datadate, fyear, cik, cusip
                   from compa.funda") %>% dbFetch,
                 y = dbSendQuery(wrds, "select gvkey, datadate, sich
                   from compa.co_industry") %>% dbFetch,
                 by = c("gvkey", "datadate")); n <- nrow(IDs)

IDs <- IDs[!duplicated(IDs), ] %>%
  filter(!is.na(fyear) & !is.na(gvkey)) %>%
  mutate(GVKEY_YEAR = paste(gvkey, fyear, sep = "_"))

IDs <- IDs %>%
  mutate(na_count = rowSums(is.na(IDs)),
         zero_count = rowSums(IDs == 0)) %>%
  arrange(na_count, zero_count) %>% distinct(GVKEY_YEAR, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(-c(GVKEY_YEAR, na_count, zero_count)); cat("Observations dropped:", n - nrow(IDs)); rm(n)

IDs <- IDs %>%
  select(GVKEY = gvkey,
         CUSIP9 = cusip,
         CIK = cik,
         TICKER = tic,
         FYEAR = fyear,
         DATE = datadate,
         SIC4 = sich) %>%
  mutate(GVKEY = as.numeric(GVKEY),
         CIK = as.numeric(CIK),
         CUSIP8 = substr(CUSIP9, 1, 8),
         DATE = format(base::as.Date(DATE, "%Y%m%d"), format = "%Y-%m"),
         SIC2 = substr(SIC4, 1, 2)) %>%
  na.omit()

IDs <- IDs %>%
  filter(!is.na(SIC4))

sic_48(IDs$SIC4, IDs$FF48_INDUSTRY)
sic_12(IDs$SIC4, IDs$FF12_INDUSTRY)

evidence.description: The commented write uses object Ravenpack, while the cleaned transformation immediately above creates Ravenpack2; later reads consume the same cleaned CSV twice.
evidence.quote:
# write_csv(Ravenpack, "Ravenpack All (Cleaned).csv")

Ravenpack <- fread("Ravenpack All (Cleaned).csv") %>% 
  mutate(YEAR = substr(DATE, 1, 4)) %>% 
  group_by(GVKEY, YEAR, ACTION) %>% 
  summarize(ACTIONS = n()) %>% 
  group_by(GVKEY, YEAR) %>%
  mutate(ACTION_VOLUME = sum(ACTIONS, na.rm = T),
         ACTION_COMPLEXITY = (ACTIONS / sum(ACTIONS, na.rm = T))^2) %>% 
  group_by(GVKEY, YEAR) %>% 
  summarize(ACTION_VOLUME = mean(ACTION_VOLUME, na.rm = T),
            ACTION_COMPLEXITY = 1 - sum(ACTION_COMPLEXITY)) %>%

  mutate(YEAR = substr(DATE, 1, 4)) %>% 
  group_by(GVKEY, YEAR, ACTION) %>%

evidence.description: The native R driver transforms Compustat annual rows into lagged growth, return, performance and five-row rolling dispersion measures.
evidence.quote:
##### IMPORT DATA: FUNDA #####
Funda <- left_join(x = dbSendQuery(wrds, "select gvkey, datadate, fyear, sale, ib, at, prcc_f, dvpsp_f, csho, ceq, ajex, ppent, che, dltt, tlcf
                   from compa.funda") %>% dbFetch,
                   y = dbSendQuery(wrds, "select datadate, gvkey, sich
                   from compa.co_industry") %>% dbFetch,
                   by = c("gvkey", "datadate")); n <- nrow(Funda)

Funda <- Funda[!duplicated(Funda), ] %>%
  filter(!is.na(fyear) & !is.na(gvkey)) %>%
  mutate(GVKEY_YEAR = paste(gvkey, fyear, sep = "_"))

Funda <- Funda %>%
  mutate(na_count = rowSums(is.na(Funda)),
         zero_count = rowSums(Funda == 0)) %>%
  arrange(na_count, zero_count) %>% distinct(GVKEY_YEAR, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(-c(GVKEY_YEAR, na_count, zero_count)); cat("Observations dropped:", n - nrow(Funda)); rm(n)

Funda <- Funda %>%
  transmute(GVKEY = as.numeric(gvkey),
            FYEAR = fyear,
            SIC4 = sich,
            SALES = sale,
            INCOME = ib,
            ASSETS = winsorize(at, 1, 99),
            PRICE = prcc_f,
            DIVIDEND = dvpsp_f,
            SHARES = csho,
            EQUITY = ceq,
            ADJUST = ajex,
            DEBT = dltt,
            PPE = ppent,
            CASH = che)

Lag_Funda <- Funda %>%
  mutate(FYEAR = FYEAR + 1,
         LAG_SALES = SALES,
         LAG_ASSETS = ASSETS,
         LAG_PRICE = PRICE,
         LAG_ADJUST = ADJUST) %>%
  select(GVKEY, FYEAR, LAG_SALES, LAG_ASSETS, LAG_PRICE, LAG_ADJUST)

Funda <- Funda %>% left_join(Lag_Funda, by = c("GVKEY", "FYEAR")); rm(Lag_Funda)

Funda <- Funda %>%
  mutate(GROWTH = (SALES - LAG_SALES) / LAG_SALES,
         
         ROA = INCOME / (ASSETS / 2 + LAG_ASSETS / 2),
         
         PRICE_ADJUST = PRICE / ADJUST,
         LAG_PRICE_ADJUST = LAG_PRICE / LAG_ADJUST,
         DIVIDEND_ADJUST = DIVIDEND / ADJUST,
         
         PPE = PPE / ASSETS,
         BTM = ASSETS / (PRICE * SHARES + ASSETS - EQUITY),
         MVE = PRICE * SHARES,
         LEVERAGE = DEBT / ASSETS,
         CASH = CASH / ASSETS,
         
         RET = (PRICE_ADJUST + DIVIDEND_ADJUST - LAG_PRICE_ADJUST) / LAG_PRICE_ADJUST)

Lag_Funda <- Funda %>%
  mutate(FYEAR = FYEAR + 1,
         LAG_ROA = ROA,
         LAG_RET = RET) %>%
  select(GVKEY, FYEAR, LAG_ROA, LAG_RET)

Funda <- Funda %>% left_join(Lag_Funda, by = c("GVKEY", "FYEAR")); rm(Lag_Funda)

Std_Perf <- Funda %>%
  select(GVKEY, FYEAR, RET, ROA) %>%
  arrange(GVKEY, FYEAR) %>%
  group_by(GVKEY) %>%
  do(data.frame(rollapplyr(.[-1], 5, by = 1, std.function, by.column = FALSE))) %>%
  ungroup %>%
  select(GVKEY, FYEAR, SD_RET, SD_ROA)

Funda <- Funda %>%
  left_join(Std_Perf,
            by = c("GVKEY", "FYEAR")); rm(Std_Perf)

Funda <- Funda %>%
  select(GVKEY, FYEAR, SALES, MVE, BTM, LEVERAGE, GROWTH, PPE, CASH, SD_ROA, ROA, LAG_ROA, SD_RET, RET, LAG_RET) %>%
  na.omit()

evidence.description: The native R driver joins CRSP monthly returns through a CCM lookup and ISS peer groups to build three-year in-sample and three-year out-of-sample windows around the annual Compustat date.
evidence.quote:
##### IMPORT DATA: RPE - PEER SYNCHRONICITY #####
CRSP <- dbSendQuery(wrds, "select date, cusip, ret
                   from crsp.msf") %>% 
  dbFetch %>% 
  rename(DATE = date,
         CUSIP8 = cusip,
         RET = ret)

CCM <- dbSendQuery(wrds2, "select gvkey, tic, lpermno, cusip
                   from crsp_a_ccm.ccm_lookup") %>%
  dbFetch %>% 
  transmute(GVKEY = gvkey %>% as.numeric,
            CUSIP8 = substr(cusip, 1, 8)) %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  unique()

CRSP <- CRSP %>% 
  left_join(CCM,
            by = "CUSIP8") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(GVKEY)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(RET)) %>% 
  select(GVKEY, DATE, RET) %>% 
  arrange(GVKEY, DATE)

Peers <- left_join(x = dbSendQuery(wrds, "select cik, fiscalyear, grantid
                   from iss_incentive_lab.gpbagrant") %>% dbFetch %>% unique(),
                   y = dbSendQuery(wrds, "select cik, grantid, peercik
                   from iss_incentive_lab.gpbarelpeer") %>% dbFetch,
                   by = c("cik", "grantid")) %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  transmute(CIK = as.numeric(cik),
            FYEAR = fiscalyear,
            PEER_CIK = as.numeric(peercik)) %>%
  unique %>%
  filter(CIK != PEER_CIK) %>% 
  arrange(CIK, FYEAR) %>% 
  left_join(IDs %>% 
              select(GVKEY, FYEAR, DATE, CIK),
            by = c("CIK", "FYEAR")) %>% 
  select(-CIK) %>% 
  rename(CIK = PEER_CIK) %>% 
  left_join(IDs %>% 
              select(PEER_GVKEY = GVKEY, FYEAR, CIK),
            by = c("CIK", "FYEAR")) %>% 
  select(GVKEY, FYEAR, PEER_GVKEY, DATE) %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  mutate(DATE = as.Date(paste0(DATE, "-01")) %m+% months(1), # beginning of next month
         DATE1 = DATE %m-% years(3),
         DATE2 = DATE %m+% years(3)) %>%
